defect_evidence: The manuscript calls this a cross-country audit without disclosing that its underlying matrix has 14 legacy-sample countries rather than the 35 current treated countries.
Only 13 audited countries overlap the current treated sample; Qatar is audit-only and 22 current treated countries were never in this source audit.
The table note does not disclose the display filter or define medium.
Chile and Saudi Arabia retain legacy source-audit entry years that differ from the current treatment target; only Australia was patched.
refuting_evidence: The producer explicitly filters the 14-country matrix to cases without an observed China cue, retaining Australia regardless; the resulting table has nine rows.
Five audited cases are hidden because their China cues were recovered: Chile, Brazil, Uruguay, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar.
Among the 26 current treated countries not displayed, four were audited and hidden by the filter and 22 were not audited; they are not a single group of omitted audit cases.
findings.reasoning: The reporting defect exists, but the review overstates the relationship between the 35-country treatment table and the nine-row display. The source audit is a 14-case legacy subset, and the display is a filtered nine-case diagnostic. Accurate disclosure resolves the present reporting problem without inventing searches for the 22 unaudited current cases.
findings.implementation_scope: Text, caption, and note only; do not change treatment rules or salience codes.

defect_evidence: Table 23 consumes a country-level summary containing only first treatment year, aggregate treated and untreated counts, and panel bounds.
The restricted risk-set producer removes post-entry off-status years and nonqualifying China-top periods, so omitted years cannot be inferred from the displayed aggregates.
The existing store contains 36 qualifying periods among 35 treated countries and 14 short excluded periods across nine of those countries, but Table 23 does not expose them.
Calendar entry-exit bounds cannot safely substitute for observed year lists because some observed periods contain calendar gaps.
findings.reasoning: The review accurately identifies a reproducibility and exposition gap. Existing target objects supply the ingredients, but producing auditable year lists and omission reasons is a new paper-facing transformation and must be implemented as targets from inception.
findings.implementation_scope: Targets-first audit outputs; no treatment-rule change; retain current table until targets exist and validate.

replacements.new: The source audit covers 14 countries from an earlier no-covariate treated sample and is not a census of the 35 countries treated in the current goods-only restricted-risk-set specification. Thirteen audited countries remain in the current treated sample; Qatar does not. The table displays the nine cases for which the China cue is coded as unknown; Chile, Brazil, Uruguay, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have recovered China cues and are omitted from this diagnostic display. For the China cue, `medium` means one countable strong or moderate first-window source with explicit rank language. For the former-incumbent benchmark, `medium` means either one countable source with explicit incumbent-rank or displacement language, or at least two countable trade-coverage records from at least one independent source without a clear top-rank label. Countable sources must be eligible, fall within one year of the source-audit entry year, be coded strong or moderate, enter the benchmark, and not be marked `DO_NOT_COUNT`. `Unknown` means that the incumbent was not identified or that no countable benchmark source was recovered; no case is currently coded `low`. Australia's displayed entry year follows the current annual goods-only panel; other entry years retain the legacy source-audit windows.
